channel.title: The Fox News Rundown
channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Midterm Post-Mortem: What the Data Reveals About Voter Frustration
item.description:
Widespread economic backlash, high fuel costs, and foreign conflict fueled historic midterm losses for the GOP across both congressional chambers. Fox News Decision Desk team member and University of Texas at Austin professor Daron Shaw joins us to break down the polling behind the Democratic sweep, unpack sharp slippage among key voting blocs like independents and Latinos, and evaluate Vice President JD Vance’s post-election autopsy ahead of 2028.
Plus, former City of Miami Mayor Francis Suarez joins to analyze how Florida remained red—even if the races were closer than expected. He also outlines how the GOP must rebuild its ground game ahead of 2028.
PHOTO CREDIT: AP  Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

item.title: Legal Fights & 'Extinction Fears': Shannon Bream on the Midterm Fallout
item.description:
Following a stunning round of midterms, the political landscape is shifting rapidly. FOX News Sunday anchor Shannon Bream joined Jessica Rosenthal on The FOX News Rundown this week to break down the immediate fallout for the Republican party, including the high-stakes scramble for House leadership between Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise, and Governor Ron DeSantis’s stark warning about the future of the GOP coalition.
Plus, Bream analyzes President Trump’s approach to upcoming congressional investigations, the shifting demographics that fractured the 2024 winning coalition, and major foreign policy hurdles ahead—from delicate trilateral talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi to upcoming high-profile meetings with China.
Finally, Bream previews her exclusive FOX News Sunday interview with New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani on the realities of progressive governance and his unique dynamic with President Trump.
We often have to cut interviews short during the week, but we thought you might like to hear the full interview.
 Today on Fox News Rundown Extra, we will share our entire interview with FOX News' Shannon Bream.
Photo Credit: House Oversight Committee

item.title: A Midterm Wave: Did Texas Just Turn Blue?
item.description:
In a stunning midterm election, voters delivered Democrats an unexpectedly dominant majority in both the House and Senate, completely obliterating the Republican Party's redistricting firewall. FOX News Chief Congressional Correspondent Chad Pergram joins the Rundown to break down what drove the results, and forecast the Democratic party’s next moves with their newfound majority.
Later, FOX News Radio Political Analyst Josh Kraushaar analyzes Democrats' sweep of Texas statewide offices, ending a 32-year Republican streak.

item.title: Progressive Democrats Set Their Sights on Corporate America
item.description:
Former staffers for Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Bernie Sanders (I-VT) say there is a 181-page roadmap being developed that urges Democrats to launch an aggressive oversight push targeting America corporations after they take control of Congress next year. The Groundwork Collaborative-backed proposal identifies hundreds of companies and executives for potential investigations, envisioning high-profile hearings where CEOs are hauled before Congress, pressed to resign, and potentially forced to provide restitution to consumers.
FOX's Eben Brown speaks with Darren Botelho, FOX Business Correspondent based in Washington D.C., who shares what this oversight plan is, and how this has the potential to cause great division amongst Democrats.

item.title: Oversight or Overreach? Potential Probes & the Battle for House Leadership
item.description:
A bruising midterm election has left House Republicans reeling and scrambling to choose new leadership as Speaker Mike Johnson steps aside and key party figures confront deep internal fractures. FOX News Sunday Anchor and host of the Livin' the Bream podcast Shannon Bream discusses the scramble between Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan for the speaker's gavel, the party debate surrounding Vice President Vance’s post-election warnings, and what the shifting balance of power means for looming Democratic investigations, Trump's foreign policy maneuvering, and the road to 2028.
Following sweeping Democratic victories in the 2026 midterms, what drove voters to abandon Republicans, and what do Democrats need to do to keep their newfound majorities? Democratic strategist and FOX News contributor Melissa DeRosa speaks with FOX News Senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy about the election results, and the challenges Democrats face as they take control of Congress. They also discuss whether Democrats can deliver on promises to lower costs and improve healthcare, and what the results could mean for the 2028 presidential race.
PLUS, commentary by FOX News contributor Joe Concha.
PHOTO CREDIT: AP IMAGES

item.title: Texas Swings Democratic for First Time in Generations
item.description:
Democrats flipped Texas blue with historic victories in governor and Senate races. Democrats pulled off twin upsets, with James Talarico defeating Attorney General Ken Paxton and Gina Hinojosa unseating Gov. Greg Abbott. The victories defied expectations in a state President Trump carried by double digits just two years earlier.
FOX's Eben Brown speaks to Josh Kraushaar, FOX News Radio political analyst and Editor-in-Chief of the Jewish Insider, who says while it was big shift for the state, he doesn't see Texas voting for a Democrat candidate for president.
